description: 21 Lessons, Get Started Building with Generative AI

summary.one_liner: A 21-lesson Microsoft beginner course teaching how to build Generative AI applications, with lessons in Python and TypeScript.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a structured course rather than a software library. It has 21 lessons, each covering its own topic, labeled either "Learn" (concept explanations) or "Build" (hands-on applications with code). Topics run from LLM fundamentals and model comparison, responsible AI, and prompt engineering to text generation, chat apps, embeddings-based search, image generation, low-code tools, function calling, UX design, security, LLMOps, RAG with vector databases, open-source models on Hugging Face, AI agents, fine-tuning, and small language models, plus Mistral and Meta model families. Each lesson includes a short video (some marked "Video Coming Soon"), a written lesson in the README, code samples for Azure OpenAI and the OpenAI API, and extra learning links. The README also lists a Course Setup lesson and translations into more than 50 languages maintained with Co-op Translator.
use_cases: build a text generation app with Azure OpenAI or OpenAI API
build a semantic search app using embeddings
build a RAG application with a vector database
build an AI agent or function calling integration
how_to_run: Fork the repository to your own GitHub account
Choose a provider: Azure OpenAI Service, Microsoft Foundry Models, OpenAI API, or Foundry Local
Follow the Course Setup lesson to prepare your development environment
notable: Each lesson is self-contained, so learners can start at any lesson
Code samples in both Python and TypeScript
Supports multiple model providers including Azure OpenAI, OpenAI API, Microsoft Foundry Models, and Foundry Local for offline use
Translations into more than 50 languages, with sparse checkout to skip them for a smaller clone
Includes a .NET edition as a separate companion course
caveats: The README says GitHub Models is retiring at the end of July 2026, so learners should use Microsoft Foundry Models instead
Several lesson videos are marked 'Video Coming Soon'
Basic knowledge of Python or TypeScript is recommended; absolute beginners are referred to separate courses
